mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 8 Series 840d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 8 Series 840d engine replacement typically costs between £2,800 and £10,500 for the engine unit alone, depending on condition type. Used B57D30 units start from around £2,800, reconditioned from £5,000, and rebuilt from £7,000. Main dealer fitted prices can reach £14,000-£18,000, while independent specialist supply & fit is significantly more competitive.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of B57 engine failure in a BMW 840d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common warning signs that your BMW 840d's B57 engine may be failing include: persistent check engine light (often EGR or DPF-related), loss of power or sluggish acceleration, rough idling, metallic rattling from the engine on cold start (timing chain), AdBlue countdown warnings that don't clear after refilling, and excessive exhaust smoke or failed MOT emissions.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 8 Series 840d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - a BMW 8 Series 840d with a failed engine is almost always worth replacing rather than scrapping. With used 840d values ranging from £27,500 to £55,000, a rebuilt engine at £7,000-£10,500 represents only 15-35% of the car's value. For a £40,000-£50,000 car that would otherwise be written off, engine replacement is financially the right decision.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 840d and 840i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 840d uses the B57 3.0-litre straight-six diesel with twin turbochargers, producing 320-340 hp and 680-700 Nm of torque. The 840i uses the B58 3.0-litre straight-six petrol engine, producing around 335 hp. The 840d delivers substantially more low-end torque (700 Nm vs ~500 Nm in the 840i) and significantly better fuel economy, making it the preferred choice for high-mileage UK drivers.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 8 Series 840d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 8 Series 840d engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist workshop to complete. The B57 engine is a straight-six mounted longitudinally with xDrive all-wheel drive, so the job requires careful drivetrain disassembly. Allow 12-16 hours of labour at independent specialist rates (£780-£1,040 at £65/hour), plus additional time for diagnostics and road testing.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a BMW 8 Series 840d rebuilt engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt BMW 8 Series 840d engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers manufacturing defects, component failure, and workmanship issues. Reconditioned engines typically come with 6-12 month warranties, while used engines usually have 3-6 month warranties or none at all. Always confirm exact terms with your chosen supplier before ordering.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 8 Series 840d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 840d's B57 diesel is broadly robust - considerably more reliable than the older N57 it replaced - but like any modern common-rail diesel, it has a handful of well-documented failure points. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: EGR Valve & DPF Clogging - Why the BMW 8 Series 840d B57D30 Suffers from Emission System Issues
problems.rootCause: Carbon deposits accumulate in the EGR valve from repeated short journeys, while the DPF struggles to reach regeneration temperature in urban driving. Both issues are driving-pattern related rather than fundamental design flaws.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean carbon deposits, or replace EGR valve assembly
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; may recur if driving habits don't change

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Software-initiated active regeneration to burn off accumulated soot
repairOptions.longevity: Works if DPF not severely blocked; requires motorway run
When EGR/DPF issues have caused secondary damage (turbo, injectors)

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A used BMW 8 Series 840d typically sits between £27,500 and £55,000 depending on year, mileage and specification. With vehicle values in the £25,000-£55,000 bracket, a full rebuilt engine at £7,000-£10,500 represents approximately 15-35% of vehicle value - well within the safe replacement threshold. Even the highest-cost rebuilt option is comfortably less than 50% of a typical 840d's market value.
problems.recommendation: For a BMW 840d with EGR or DPF issues but no secondary damage, the specialist EGR clean or forced regeneration is the sensible first step. If the car has covered over 100,000 miles and you plan to keep it, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components offers better long-term value than repeated emission-system repairs.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B57D30 BMW 8 Series 840d engine prices

problems.h4: AdBlue System Failure - BMW 840d SCR Emission Control Problems
problems.rootCause: The selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system relies on AdBlue fluid injected into the exhaust. NOx sensors, metering valves, heaters and the SCR pump can all fail - often crystallisation of AdBlue or electrical faults.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Refill AdBlue tank and reset countdown via diagnostic tool
repairOptions.longevity: If warning is simply low fluid - always try this first

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty NOx sensor, clear fault codes
repairOptions.longevity: Common fix for P20EE / P207F codes

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace metering valve, pump or heater assembly

repairOptions.longevity: Only if AdBlue failure has led to wider engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - BMW 840d values of £27,500-£55,000 mean full engine replacement remains financially viable even with the premium rebuilt option.
problems.recommendation: AdBlue system faults on the BMW 840d are frustrating but rarely engine-ending. Start with a diagnostic check from a BMW diesel specialist - many AdBlue issues are sensor-related rather than mechanical. If the system has been ignored and the countdown has expired, the car may refuse to start, so address AdBlue warnings immediately.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B57D30B BMW 8 Series 840d engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Wear - BMW 840d B57 Chain Durability
problems.rootCause: Unlike the older N47 and N57 engines with well-documented timing chain failures, the B57's timing chain is notably more robust and durable. However, chain stretch can still occur over very high mileage, particularly in higher-output variants.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Visual inspection and tensioner check via diagnostic access
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended at 100k miles as preventative check

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, guides, tensioners (full B57 timing chain kit)
repairOptions.longevity: If rattling on startup or misfire codes present
If chain has snapped or caused valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: With BMW 840d values starting at £27,500, even the full rebuild option at £10,500 is only ~38% of the lowest used value. Replacement is financially justified on all but the highest-mileage, lowest-spec examples.
problems.recommendation: The B57 timing chain is significantly more reliable than its predecessors, but if you hear a metallic rattle from the engine on cold start - particularly between 100,000 and 150,000 miles - have it inspected immediately. Early tensioner replacement (around £1,500-£2,500 at specialist rates) is far cheaper than a full engine rebuild if the chain snaps.
